questions.question: In a discussion of religious identity before British colonial census-taking, one speaker describes a transactional, patchily integrated pre-colonial world using a paired set of adjectives. What are the two adjectives used together to describe this world?
questions.rationale: This paragraph is the only place in the corpus pairing 'Islamisate' and 'Indic' to describe the pre-colonial world of intermingled devotion.

questions.question: One interview describes an author who was voted onto a global ideas platform's list of '33 Entrepreneurs Who Make The World A Better Place,' and whose second-named book won an award in 2018. Name the platform and the award.
questions.rationale: Only this paragraph names IdeaMensch as the platform and the Wilbur Award as the 2018 prize for the interviewee's second book.

questions.question: One essay compares several 20th-century national ideologies to their dreams — the Nazi's superman, Mussolini's revived empire, the communists' New Mass Man — before turning to a freedom leader whose vision was a republic of autonomous villages living an 'Arcadian life' close to nature. Name that leader and the book in which he set out this vision.
questions.rationale: This paragraph's list of national ideological dreams closes with Gandhi and Hind Swaraj, distinguishing it from generic discussions of the same leader.

questions.question: A biting critique of society women's meetings says they arrive in fancy shawls and embroidered turbans, get through 'a whole ton of supari nuts' and 'cartloads of betel leaves' — and then use up a tank full of what, before going home having accomplished nothing?
questions.rationale: The quoted critique's specific list of consumed items, ending in a tank of rosewater, appears only in this paragraph.

questions.question: An essay on traditional Indian values for regulating economic and desire-satisfying activities coins two adjectives — one for wealth-and-income-acquiring activities, one for want-satisfying activities. What are they called?
questions.rationale: The coined terms Arthic and Kamic, for the two categories of daily activity, appear only in this paragraph.

questions.question: A reflection on India's 1977 election victory refers to the winning coalition not simply as the Janata Party but by a compound name including another party's initials. What was that compound name?
questions.rationale: The compound name 'Janata-CFD party' for the 1977 winning coalition appears only in this paragraph.

questions.question: A piece on the 1962 border war states that the Dalai Lama and his followers were driven out of Tibet by Chinese forces in a specific year — earlier than the year usually cited. What year does the piece give, and what dismissive epithet does it use for the Chinese forces occupying Tibet?
questions.rationale: This paragraph's idiosyncratic 1960 dating of the Dalai Lama's exile and its 'Red bandits' epithet appear together only here.

questions.question: A social worker born in Cuttack on 3 December 1899, daughter of Basanta Kumari Devi and Gopal Ballav Das, was the niece of a lawyer and social reformer honoured with the title 'Utkal Gaurab' for his role in unifying Odisha. Name that reformer.
questions.rationale: This paragraph is the only place naming Madhusudhan Das as the profiled woman's uncle.

questions.question: An essay on property rights over river water gives an example of a ghost town on the banks of the Yamuna, 40 km from Dehra Doon, whose irrigation department owns the town but is broke. Name the town.
questions.rationale: Dakpathar is named as the specific ghost town only in this paragraph.

questions.question: A woman born on 2 February 1889 into the royal family of Kapurthala was introduced to nationalist politics through Gopal Krishna Gokhale's influence on her father. Name her father, as given in the profile.
questions.rationale: This paragraph is the only place naming Harnam Singh Ahluwalia as her father, connected to Gokhale's influence.
